title.en: King Huan of Zhou dies; his son King Zhuang of Zhou, Ji Tuo, ascends the throne

summary.en: In 697 BCE, King Huan of Zhou, Ji Lin, died. During his 23-year reign, he repeatedly fought with Zheng, and the authority of the Son of Heaven further declined. His son Ji Tuo succeeded him as King Zhuang of Zhou. statement.zh: 公元前697年，周桓王姬林去世，其在位23年间屡次与郑国交战，天子权威进一步衰落。其子姬佗继位，是为周庄王。庄王虽试图重整王权，但诸侯国已纷纷自立，王室实际控制的土地和兵力十分有限。
statement.en:
In 697 BCE, King Huan of Zhou, Ji Lin, died. During his 23-year reign, he repeatedly fought with Zheng, and the authority of the Son of Heaven further declined. His son Ji Tuo succeeded him as King Zhuang of Zhou. Although King Zhuang tried to restore royal power, the vassal states had already become independent, and the land and troops under the royal house's actual control were very limited.

For Asia in 697 BCE, “King Huan of Zhou dies; his son King Zhuang of Zhou, Ji Tuo, ascends the throne” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

zh: 公元前697年，周桓王姬林去世，其在位23年间屡次与郑国交战，天子权威进一步衰落。其子姬佗继位，是为周庄王。庄王虽试图重整王权，但诸侯国已纷纷自立，王室实际控制的土地和兵力十分有限。
公元前697年，周桓王姬林去世，其在位23年间屡次与郑国交战，天子权威进一步衰落。
en: In 697 BCE, King Huan of Zhou, Ji Lin, died. During his 23-year reign, he repeatedly fought with Zheng, and the authority of the Son of Heaven further declined. His son Ji Tuo succeeded him as King Zhuang of Zhou. Although King Zhuang tried to restore royal power, the vassal states had already become independent, and the land and troops under the royal house's actual control were very limited.
In 697 BCE, King Huan of Zhou, Ji Lin, died.

title.en: Early Iron Age begins in Central Europe's Hallstatt culture

summary.en: In Central Europe, the Hallstatt civilization began to widely use iron tools, replacing bronze. Iron smelting technology spread from the Mediterranean, boosting agricultural productivity and weapons innovation.

statement.zh:
中欧地区哈尔施塔特文明开始普遍使用铁器，取代青铜工具，冶铁技术从地中海传入，推动农业生产力和武器革新。铁制农具提高了耕作效率，铁剑与盔甲改变了战斗方式；墓葬中的器物与贸易品显示与地中海的联系。

把「欧洲中欧哈尔施塔特文化进入铁器时代初期」放回公元前696年的中欧，可以看到科技变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en: The Hallstatt civilization in Central Europe began to widely use iron tools instead of bronze tools.

title.en: King Zhuang of Zhou newly enthroned; civil strife in Wei: princes Xie and Zhi attack and kill Duke Hui of Wei

summary.en: In 696 BCE, Duke Hui of Wei had usurped the throne earlier, causing widespread discontent among the clan. With King Zhuang of Zhou newly established, Prince Xie and Prince Zhi allied with the people of Wei to launch a coup and kill Duke Hui. Duke Hui fled to Qi. Wei then fell into years of succession wars.

title.en: Duke Huan of Lu meets Duke Xiang of Qi at Luo; Duke Huan of Lu is murdered by Duke Xiang of Qi

summary.en: Duke Huan of Lu brought his wife Wen Jiang (sister of Duke Xiang of Qi) to Qi. Duke Xiang of Qi had an affair with Wen Jiang and ordered the strongman Gongzi Pengsheng to pull Duke Huan to death in his chariot. Lu dared not seek revenge but only demanded Pengsheng's life; Duke Xiang killed Pengsheng to cover up the matter.

statement.zh: 鲁桓公携夫人文姜（齐襄公妹）赴齐，齐襄公与文姜通奸，命公子彭生力大将其拉杀于车中。鲁国不敢兴师问罪，仅要求彭生抵罪，齐襄公杀彭生搪塞。

title.en: Assyrian king Sennacherib orders the rebuilding of Babylon

summary.en: A few years after completely destroying Babylon, Sennacherib decided to rebuild the Esagila temple and the city, and grant Babylon a degree of autonomy to pacify the people and gods of Babylonia.

statement.zh:
辛那赫里布在彻底摧毁巴比伦几年后，为安抚巴比伦尼亚民众及众神，决定重建埃萨吉拉神庙和城池，并赐予巴比伦一定自治权。亚述以重建换取祭司集团与城市的顺从，同时保留驻军与税权；马尔杜克神的祭祀恢复，旧都的宗教中心地位得以延续。

把「亚述王辛那赫里布下令重建巴比伦城」放回公元前693年的亚述，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en: A few years after Sennacherib completely destroyed Babylon, in order to appease the Babylonian people and gods, he decided to rebuild the temple and city of Esagira and grant Babylon a certain degree of autonomy.

title.en: Elamite king Shutruk-Nakhunte II invades northern Babylon

summary.en: Taking advantage of the Assyrian main force fighting in the west, the Elamites raided northern Babylonian cities and plundered large amounts of goods. The Assyrian garrison was unable to counter effectively, causing continued instability in Mesopotamia.

statement.zh:
趁亚述主力在西线作战，埃兰人突袭巴比伦北部城市，劫掠大量财物，亚述驻军未能有效反击，导致两河流域动荡持续。两河平原城市密集、边界交错，突袭易于得手却难以长期占据；亚述多线作战暴露了兵力调配的困难。地区秩序因此在震荡中重组。

把「埃兰国王舒特鲁克·纳克杭特二世入侵巴比伦北部」放回公元前692年的埃兰，可以看到军事变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Assyrian king Sennacherib campaigns against Arabian desert tribes

summary.en: Arabian tribes had long harassed Assyrian trade routes. Sennacherib led a camel cavalry deep into the desert, defeated the Qedarites and others, seized water sources, and forced the Arab chieftains to pay tribute.

title.en: Assyrian king Sennacherib suppresses Babylonian rebellion

summary.en: Babylonian nobles allied with Elamites to rebel against Assyria. Sennacherib marched south and in 689 BCE destroyed Babylon, massacred its inhabitants, and diverted the Euphrates to flood the ruins. This extreme action caused strong discontent among Assyrian religious circles and is considered one of the reasons for his later assassination.

statement.zh: 巴比伦贵族联合埃兰人反叛亚述。辛那赫里布率军南下，于公元前689年摧毁巴比伦城，屠戮居民，并引幼发拉底河水淹没废墟。这一极端行为导致亚述国内宗教人士强烈不满，被认为是他后来被弑的原因之一。

title.en: Assyrian king Sennacherib moves capital to Nineveh and expands the 'Palace Without Rival'

summary.en: To avoid the impact of Babylonian rebellions, Sennacherib formally moved the capital from Kalakh to Nineveh, launched large-scale construction of palaces, and dug canals to bring water into the city. Nineveh became one of the largest cities in the world at that time.

statement.zh: 为避免巴比伦叛乱影响，辛那赫里布正式将都城从卡拉赫迁往尼尼微，大兴土木建造宫殿，并开凿运河引水入城，尼尼微成为当时世界最大城市之一。宫殿以浮雕与门兽装饰，宣示帝国的武功与秩序；运河与城墙把水源、仓储与防务连成一体。迁都把亚述的政治重心北移。
statement.en: In order to avoid the influence of the Babylonian rebellion, Sennacherib officially moved the capital from Carach to Nineveh, built a palace on a large scale, and dug canals to divert water into the city.

title.en: Athens abolishes lifelong archonship and establishes ten-year archons

summary.en: In 682 BCE, tensions between Athenian nobles and commoners intensified. To limit the power of the archons and prevent personal rule, Athens abolished the lifelong archonship and replaced it with a ten-year term. Archons were still elected by the aristocracy, and commoners had no right to vote. This reform was an important step in Athens' transition to democracy.

title.en: Duke Huan of Qi convenes the first interstate meeting at Beixing with Song, Chen, Cai, and Zhu

title.en: Esarhaddon orders full reconstruction of Babylon and releases deported inhabitants

summary.en: To fulfill his promise, Esarhaddon allocated Assyrian treasury funds to repair Babylon's temples and walls and allowed exiled Babylonians to return. Babylon once again submitted to Assyria.

statement.zh:
为兑现承诺，以撒哈顿从亚述国库拨款修复巴比伦神庙和城墙，并允许流亡的巴比伦人返乡，巴比伦重新臣服于亚述。重建既是宗教义务，也是政治安抚：恢复神庙与祭祀可争取巴比伦祭司与贵族，返乡则恢复城市的经济与社会结构。亚述以怀柔补充武力。

title.en: Gyges Becomes King of Lydia, Founding a New Dynasty

summary.en: Gyges came to power in Lydia through a coup, founding the Mermnad dynasty. The traditional dating of Gyges' reign is around 680–644 BCE. He strengthened trade relations with Assyria and the Greek poleis, and introduced Greek mercenaries. Lydia's prosperity laid the foundation for the later glory of Croesus.

statement.zh: 巨吉斯（Gyges）通过政变成为吕底亚国王，创立马格涅斯王朝。传统年代巨吉斯在位约为公元前680-644年。他加强了与亚述帝国和希腊城邦的贸易关系，引进希腊雇佣兵。吕底亚的繁荣为后来克洛伊索斯时代的辉煌奠定基础。
statement.en: Gyges came to power in Lydia through a coup, founding the Mermnad dynasty.

title.en: Duke Huan of Qi helps rebuild Wei; feudal lords formally recognize Qi as hegemon

summary.en: The Di tribes destroyed Wei; only 700 Wei refugees survived. Duke Huan of Qi led allied forces to expel the Di, rebuilt the city at Chuqiu, and installed Duke Dai of Wei. The feudal lords thus honored Duke Huan of Qi as the overlord (Bo).

statement.zh:
狄人灭卫，卫遗民七百余人逃亡。齐桓公率诸侯军队驱逐狄人，在楚丘重新筑城，立卫戴公，诸侯由此尊齐桓公为伯主。存亡继绝的行动把齐的武力转为礼制号召，诸侯在周室衰微时寻求秩序；齐以会盟与救患确立霸主地位。霸政由此获得合法性。

把「齐桓公帮助卫国重建，诸侯正式推齐为霸主」放回公元前679年的齐，可以看到外交变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Quwo Wugong attacks and kills Marquis Jin of Jin, unifies Jin; King Xi of Zhou appoints him ruler of Jin

summary.en: After three generations of effort, Quwo Wugong killed Marquis Jin and bribed the Zhou king with captured treasures. King Xi appointed Wugong as ruler of Jin, ending the long-standing internal division of Jin.

statement.zh:
曲沃武公经过三代努力，杀晋侯缗，用掠夺的宝器贿赂周王，周僖王册封武公为晋君，是为晋武公，结束晋国内部长期分裂。曲沃一支以小宗蚕食大宗，逐步夺取晋国都城与土地；周王受赂而命，等于承认既成事实，礼制秩序因此松动。晋国由此转入强盛之路。

把「曲沃武公攻灭晋侯缗，统一晋国，周僖王命为晋君」放回公元前678年的晋，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Assyrian king Esarhaddon campaigns against Phoenicia, captures Sidon

summary.en: The Phoenician city-state of Sidon allied with Egypt to resist Assyria. Esarhaddon besieged Sidon for three years with navy and army, then sacked the city and rebuilt a new Sidon as an Assyrian port.

statement.zh:
腓尼基城邦西顿联合埃及反抗亚述，以撒哈顿率海军和陆军包围西顿三年，破城后屠城并重建新西顿作为亚述港口。围城切断海上补给，攻城器械与土垒推进至城墙；城破后的重建把西顿纳入亚述的贸易体系。此役显示亚述对东地中海沿岸的控制。

把「亚述王以撒哈顿远征腓尼基，占领西顿」放回公元前677年的腓尼基，可以看到军事变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en: The Phoenician city-state of Sidon allied with Egypt to resist Assyria.

title.en: King Hui of Zhou restored; Zheng and Guo put down Prince Tui's rebellion

summary.en: Prince Tui, allied with Wei and Yan, seized the royal city and falsely claimed the throne. Duke Li of Zheng and Duke of Guo united to restore King Hui of Zhou, but the king's authority was again severely damaged.

statement.zh:
王子颓勾结卫、燕国攻占王城，僭称周王。郑厉公和虢公联合勤王，杀王子颓，迎周惠王复位，但周王权威再受重创。王室内争与诸侯干涉交织，勤王之举既是尊王，也是诸侯借机扩张影响；复位之后，王室对畿内与礼仪的控制进一步削弱。东周的王权由此更依赖强国。

把「周惠王复辟，郑、虢二国平定王子颓之乱」放回公元前676年的东周，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。

statement.zh: 公元前675年，楚文王以息侯对楚国不敬为借口出兵灭掉了息国（今河南息县）。息侯夫人息妫（息夫人）以美貌闻名，被楚文王纳入后宫。息妫虽在后宫生下两个儿子却终日不语，楚文王问其原因她回答："一个女人侍奉两个丈夫，即使不死，还有什么话可说？"。
statement.en:
In 675 BCE, King Wen of Chu used the excuse that the Marquis of Xi had shown disrespect to Chu to attack and destroy Xi (in present-day Xi County, Henan). Lady Xi Gui (Lady Xi), famous for her beauty, was taken into the Chu king's harem. Although she bore two sons, she remained silent. When asked why, she replied, 'A woman serving two husbands—even if she does not die, what is there to say?'

title.en: Roman king Servius Tullius implements military and political reforms

summary.en: Servius Tullius divided citizens into five classes based on property, determining the number of soldiers each class had to provide. He also established the Centuriate Assembly, breaking the aristocracy's monopoly on military power and laying the foundation for the Roman Republic.

statement.zh: 塞尔维乌斯按财产划分公民为五个等级，确定各等级提供军队数量，并建立百人队会议，打破贵族垄断兵权，为罗马共和国制度奠定基础。
statement.en:
Servius Tullius divided citizens into five classes based on property, determining the number of soldiers each class had to provide. He also established the Centuriate Assembly, breaking the aristocracy's monopoly on military power and laying the foundation for the Roman Republic.

For Europe in 673 BCE, “Roman king Servius Tullius implements military and political reforms” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Assyrian king Esarhaddon appoints his eldest son Ashurbanipal as crown prince and second son Shamash-shum-ukin as king of Babylon

summary.en: To prevent rivalry among his sons, Esarhaddon decreed that Ashurbanipal would inherit Assyria proper and Shamash would rule Babylon. However, the brothers later turned against each other, leading to a major rebellion in Babylon.

statement.zh:
为避免儿子争位，以撒哈顿立约：亚述巴尼拔继承亚述本土，沙马什统治巴比伦，但兄弟后来反目，导致巴比伦大叛乱。分治安排试图以嫡庶与封地划定权责，却难以消解继承竞争；巴比伦的宗教与城市传统又使副王拥有独立根基。王室内讧最终削弱帝国。

title.en: Assyria expels Kushite pharaohs

title.en: Esarhaddon conquers Egypt; Memphis falls

summary.en: The Assyrian army crossed the Sinai Peninsula, defeated the Egyptian pharaoh Taharqa at the Battle of Ishqupu, and occupied Memphis. Taharqa fled south, and Assyria directly ruled Egypt for the first time.

title.en: Assyrian king Esarhaddon dies; Ashurbanipal ascends

summary.en: In 669 BCE, King Esarhaddon of the Assyrian Empire died on his way back from Egypt to Nineveh. His son Ashurbanipal succeeded him. Ashurbanipal was the last great king of Assyria. He established the famous library at Nineveh, which collected thousands of cuneiform tablets. He immediately faced a rebellion by his brother Shamash-shum-ukin in Babylon.

statement.zh: 公元前669年，亚述帝国的以撒哈顿王在从埃及返回尼尼微的途中病逝。其子亚述巴尼拔继承王位。亚述巴尼拔是亚述最后一位伟大的君主，在尼尼微建立了著名的图书馆，收藏了大量楔形文字泥板文献。但他立即面临其弟弟沙马什-舒姆-乌金在巴比伦发动的叛乱。
statement.en:
In 669 BCE, King Esarhaddon of the Assyrian Empire died on his way back from Egypt to Nineveh. His son Ashurbanipal succeeded him. Ashurbanipal was the last great king of Assyria. He established the famous library at Nineveh, which collected thousands of cuneiform tablets. He immediately faced a rebellion by his brother Shamash-shum-ukin in Babylon.

For Asia in 669 BCE, “Assyrian king Esarhaddon dies; Ashurbanipal ascends” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

公元前669年，亚述帝国的以撒哈顿王在从埃及返回尼尼微的途中病逝。
en: In 669 BCE, King Esarhaddon of the Assyrian Empire died on his way back from Egypt to Nineveh. His son Ashurbanipal succeeded him. Ashurbanipal was the last great king of Assyria. He established the famous library at Nineveh, which collected thousands of cuneiform tablets. He immediately faced a rebellion by his brother Shamash-shum-ukin in Babylon.
In 669 BCE, King Esarhaddon of the Assyrian Empire died on his way back from Egypt to Nineveh.

title.en: Ashurbanipal campaigns against Arabia, destroys oasis cities

summary.en: In 665 BCE, Ashurbanipal led an expedition into northern Arabia. Arabian nomadic tribes had cut off Assyrian trade routes and refused to submit. The Assyrian army penetrated the desert, captured the oasis cities of Tayma and Dedan, and plundered vast numbers of camels and gold and silver. After the campaign, the Arabian tribes were forced to resubmit to Assyria.

statement.zh: 公元前665年，亚述巴尼拔率军远征阿拉伯半岛北部。阿拉伯游牧部族切断了亚述的商路并拒绝称臣纳贡。亚述军队深入沙漠攻占了泰马、迪丹等绿洲城市，掠走了大量的骆驼和金银财宝。远征后阿拉伯各部落被迫重新臣服于亚述。
statement.en: In 665 BCE, Ashurbanipal led an expedition into northern Arabia.

title.en: Duke Huan of Qi campaigns north against the Shanrong, saving Yan

summary.en: The Shanrong attacked Yan; Duke Zhuang of Yan sought help from Qi. Duke Huan of Qi led an army north, reaching as far as Guzhu (present-day Lulong, Hebei), defeated the Shanrong, and donated the captured land to Yan, ensuring Yan's survival.

statement.zh:
山戎攻燕，燕庄公向齐求救。齐桓公率军北伐，远至孤竹国（今河北卢龙），击败山戎，将所得土地赠燕，燕国得以存续。出兵把诸侯救援与霸政秩序联系起来，远征的后勤与地形考验军队；战后以土地相赠，既固边又树立号召力。

title.en: Egyptian pharaoh Taharqa dies; Tantamani ascends; Assyria again invades Egypt and sacks Thebes

summary.en: In 664 BCE, Kushite pharaoh Taharqa (25th Dynasty) died, and his nephew Tantamani succeeded. Tantamani tried to recapture Lower Egypt from Assyria. Ashurbanipal sent a large army south, which captured and sacked Thebes, looting vast amounts of gold. The 25th Dynasty ended.

title.en: Megarian colonists found Byzantium

summary.en: In 660 BCE, Greek colonists from Megara, led by Byzas, founded Byzantium on the European side of the Bosporus Strait. Its location was extremely strategic, controlling the passage between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean. Byzantium later developed into a major commercial center and became Constantinople, the new capital of the Roman Empire, in 330 CE.

title.en: Di destroy Wei; Duke Huan of Qi rescues Wei and moves its capital to Chuqiu

title.en: Duke Cheng of Qin dies; his brother Duke Mu of Qin (Renhao) ascends

summary.en: In 659 BCE, Duke Cheng of Qin died. Having no sons, his younger brother Renhao succeeded him as Duke Mu of Qin. Duke Mu reigned from 659 to 621 BCE. He employed worthy ministers such as Baili Xi, Jian Shu, and You Yu, expanded west, conquered the Rong tribes, and became the hegemon of the western regions, laying a solid foundation for Qin's eventual unification of China.

statement.zh: 公元前659年，秦成公去世。因成公无子，其弟任好继位，是为秦穆公。秦穆公在位期间（前659-前621年）任用百里奚、蹇叔、由余等贤臣，向西发展征服西戎各国，称霸西戎，成为春秋五霸之一，为秦国日后统一天下奠定了坚实基础。
statement.en:
In 659 BCE, Duke Cheng of Qin died. Having no sons, his younger brother Renhao succeeded him as Duke Mu of Qin. Duke Mu reigned from 659 to 621 BCE. He employed worthy ministers such as Baili Xi, Jian Shu, and You Yu, expanded west, conquered the Rong tribes, and became the hegemon of the western regions, laying a solid foundation for Qin's eventual unification of China.

For Asia in 659 BCE, “Duke Cheng of Qin dies; his brother Duke Mu of Qin (Renhao) ascends” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Corinthian tyrant Cypselus overthrows the Bacchiadae aristocracy and establishes tyranny

summary.en: The Bacchiadae family had long monopolized power in Corinth. Cypselus, with the support of commoners and merchants, launched a coup around 657 BCE, overthrowing the aristocracy and becoming the first tyrant of Corinth. He greatly developed trade and colonization, making Corinth one of the most prosperous Greek city-states. His son Periander continued Corinth's golden age.

title.en: Duke Huan of Qi leads eight-state coalition against Chu; Chu envoy Qu Wan concludes alliance at Shaoling

summary.en: The Qi-led coalition advanced to Mount Xing. King Cheng of Chu sent Qu Wan to negotiate at Shaoling. Qu Wan said, 'If you, my lord, rule the vassals by virtue, who would dare not submit?' Duke Huan, seeing that the Chu army was in good order, made peace with Chu, and Chu recognized Qi's hegemony.

statement.zh:
齐率联军进军陉山，楚成王派屈完赴召陵谈判。屈完说：“君若以德绥诸侯，谁敢不服？”齐桓公见楚军阵整，遂与楚盟，楚承认齐霸主地位。会盟以军威与辞令交锋，双方在实力与礼制之间妥协；霸主秩序靠盟誓与威慑维持。齐楚关系由此暂时稳定。

statement.en: The meeting pitted military display against rhetoric, and the two sides compromised between power and ritual; hegemonic order rested on oaths and deterrence.

title.en: Ashurbanipal establishes a great library at Nineveh, collecting cuneiform tablets

summary.en: Ashurbanipal sent scholars to Babylonia to copy ancient texts, collecting tens of thousands of clay tablets containing epics, science, and religion, preserving much of Mesopotamian knowledge for posterity.

statement.zh: 亚述巴尼拔派遣学者前往巴比伦尼亚抄写古代文献，收藏数万块泥板，内容包括史诗、科学、宗教，为后世保存了大量美索不达米亚文明知识。
statement.en: Ashurbanipal sent scholars to Babylonia to copy ancient documents and collected tens of thousands of clay tablets, including epics, science, and religion, and preserved a large amount of Mesopotamian civilization knowledge for future generations.

sources.locator: Wikipedia, "Library of Ashurbanipal", full article, evidence sentence 1
sources.excerpt: The Royal Library of Ashurbanipal, named after Ashurbanipal, the last great king of the Assyrian Empire, is a collection of more than 30,000 clay tablets and fragments containing texts of all kinds and in various languages from the 7th century BCE.

en: Ashurbanipal sent scholars to Babylonia to copy ancient documents and collected tens of thousands of clay tablets, including epics, science, and religion, and preserved a large amount of Mesopotamian civilization knowledge for future generations.

title.en: Elamite king Te-hum-um-Igigi is captured by Assyria; Elam becomes a vassal

summary.en: In 653 BCE, Assyrian king Ashurbanipal invaded Elam (present-day southwestern Iran) and defeated the Elamite army at the Battle of Dur-Untash, capturing King Te-hum-um-Igigi. title.en: Babylonian king Shamash-shum-ukin allies with Elam and Chaldea to rebel against Assyria

summary.en: In 652 BCE, Ashurbanipal's brother, the Babylonian king Shamash-shum-ukin, allied with Elam, the Chaldeans, Arab tribes, and parts of Syria to launch a major rebellion against Assyria. The rebels controlled most of Babylonia and cut communications between the two rivers. Ashurbanipal mobilized his main army to counterattack and besieged Babylon for two years.

statement.zh: 公元前652年，亚述巴尼拔的弟弟、巴比伦国王沙马什·舒姆·乌金联合埃兰、迦勒底人、阿拉伯部落和部分叙利亚地区发动大规模的叛亚述战争。
statement.en: In 652 BCE, Ashurbanipal's brother, the Babylonian king Shamash-shum-ukin, allied with Elam, the Chaldeans, Arab tribes, and parts of Syria to launch a major rebellion against Assyria.

sources.excerpt: Shamash-shum-ukin (flourished 7th century bc) was the crown prince of Babylon, son of Esarhaddon and brother of Ashurbanipal the last of the great kings of Assyria. He led a coalition of Arabic tribes against Ashurbanipal, but, after being starved out by his brother’s siege of Babylon (684 bc), he capitulated. According to tradition, Shamash-shum-ukin committed suicide by making a pyre of his palace, treasury, and concubines.

zh: 公元前652年，亚述巴尼拔的弟弟、巴比伦国王沙马什·舒姆·乌金联合埃兰、迦勒底人、阿拉伯部落和部分叙利亚地区发动大规模的叛亚述战争。
en: In 652 BCE, Ashurbanipal's brother, the Babylonian king Shamash-shum-ukin, allied with Elam, the Chaldeans, Arab tribes, and parts of Syria to launch a major rebellion against Assyria.

title.en: Duke Mu of Qin supports Prince Yiwu's return to Jin to ascend the throne

summary.en: After Duke Xian of Jin died and the Li Ji turmoil, Yiwu sought Qin's help to return, promising to cede the Hexi region. Duke Mu of Qin sent troops to escort Yiwu back to Jin, where he became Duke Hui of Jin. However, Duke Hui reneged on his promise and did not cede the land.

statement.zh:
晋献公去世，骊姬之乱后夷吾求秦助返国，许诺割河西之地。秦穆公派兵护送夷吾回国，是为晋惠公，但惠公背约不割地。援立以土地为酬，君臣信义由此受损；秦国借护送介入晋国政局，晋惠公则因失信而难以服众。两国关系在恩怨中反复。

把「秦穆公支援晋惠公回国即位」放回公元前649年的晋，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en:
After Duke Xian of Jin died and the Li Ji turmoil, Yiwu sought Qin's help to return, promising to cede the Hexi region. Duke Mu of Qin sent troops to escort Yiwu back to Jin, where he became Duke Hui of Jin. However, Duke Hui reneged on his promise and did not cede the land. Support for the accession was paid for in land, and trust between ruler and minister suffered; Qin intervened in Jin's politics through the escort, while Duke Hui could hardly command loyalty after breaking faith. Relations between the two states swung between grievance and reconciliation.

Placing “Duke Mu of Qin supports Prince Yiwu's return to Jin to ascend the throne” in 649 BCE Asia shows one concrete slice of Politics change.

title.en: Ashurbanipal captures Babylon; his brother Shamash-shum-ukin commits suicide by fire

summary.en: After a long siege, the Assyrian army broke into Babylon. The rebel king Shamash-shum-ukin set himself on fire in his palace. Ashurbanipal sacked the city in revenge, and Babylon lost all independence.

title.en: Median king Phraortes attacks northern Assyria, is defeated and killed

summary.en: The Median kingdom began to expand. Phraortes led an army against Assyrian Nineveh but was routed by the Assyrians and killed. His son Cyaxares succeeded him.

statement.zh:
米底王国开始扩张，弗拉欧尔特斯率军进攻亚述的尼尼微，被亚述军击溃，弗拉欧尔特斯阵亡，其子基亚克萨雷斯继位。米底由部落联盟向王权国家转变，扩张却撞上亚述的军事优势；君主阵亡使部族重新整合。继任者继续积蓄力量。

把「米底国王弗拉欧尔特斯进攻亚述北部，战败被杀」放回公元前646年的米底，可以看到军事变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: The Library of Nineveh is completed, becoming the largest repository of knowledge in the ancient world

summary.en: Ashurbanipal ordered over 20,000 clay tablets collected from various places to be stored in the Nineveh palace, classified by subject, including grammar, medicine, astronomy, and the Epic of Gilgamesh.

statement.zh:
亚述巴尼拔下令将各地搜集的两万多块泥板存入尼尼微宫殿，按学科分类，包括语法、医学、天文学和史诗《吉尔伽美什》。泥板以楔形文字书写，抄写员整理巴比伦传统；王室藏书兼有行政档案与知识汇编的性质。图书馆把征服所得转化为可保存的知识。

把「尼尼微图书馆最终完工，成为古代世界最大知识宝库」放回公元前645年的亚述，可以看到文化变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Li Ji turmoil in Jin: Crown Prince Shensheng commits suicide; Chong'er and Yiwu flee

summary.en: Duke Xian of Jin's favored concubine Li Ji wanted her son Xiqi to be heir. She falsely accused Crown Prince Shensheng of poisoning Duke Xian. Shensheng hanged himself at Xincheng. Chong'er fled to Pu, and Yiwu fled to Qu, sparking civil war in Jin.

statement.zh:
晋献公宠妃骊姬欲立其子奚齐，诬陷太子申生毒害献公。申生自缢于新城。重耳奔蒲，夷吾奔屈，晋国内乱爆发。献公死后，奚齐与卓子相继被杀，诸公子流亡；晋国在继承问题上长期动荡，直至重耳归国。

把「晋国骊姬之乱，太子申生自杀，重耳夷吾出奔」放回公元前645年的晋，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: King Cheng of Chu attacks Xu; Duke Huan of Qi leads allied forces to relieve Xu

summary.en: In 644 BCE, King Cheng of Chu, seeking to expand north, attacked Xu (present-day Si County, Anhui). Xu was an eastern member of the Central Plains alliance. Hegemon Duke Huan of Qi consequently led a coalition of Lu, Song, Chen, Wei, Zheng, Xu, Cao, and others to rescue Xu. The allied forces confronted the Chu army on Xu's border for months, and the Chu army eventually withdrew

statement.zh: 公元前644年，楚成王为扩张势力北上讨伐徐国（今安徽泗县）。徐国是中原联盟的东方成员，齐国霸主齐桓公随即联合鲁、宋、陈、卫、郑、许、曹等诸侯国出兵救徐。诸侯联军与楚军在徐国边境对峙数月，楚军最终撤兵。齐桓公此次成功救援维护了中原联盟的团结。
statement.en:
In 644 BCE, King Cheng of Chu, seeking to expand north, attacked Xu (present-day Si County, Anhui). Xu was an eastern member of the Central Plains alliance. Hegemon Duke Huan of Qi consequently led a coalition of Lu, Song, Chen, Wei, Zheng, Xu, Cao, and others to rescue Xu. The allied forces confronted the Chu army on Xu's border for months, and the Chu army eventually withdrew. This successful rescue maintained unity among the Central Plains alliance.

For Asia in 644 BCE, “King Cheng of Chu attacks Xu; Duke Huan of Qi leads allied forces to relieve Xu” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Rome goes to war with the Latin League; Rome gradually takes control of the Latin plain

summary.en: To gain control of Alba Longa's legacy, Rome clashed with cities of the Latin League. King Tullius of Rome, after several battles, forced some Latin cities to accept Roman hegemony.

statement.zh: 罗马为了争夺阿尔巴隆加遗产，与拉丁同盟各城爆发冲突。罗马国王图利乌斯经过多次战斗，迫使部分拉丁城接受罗马霸权，拉丁平原上的城邦格局因此改观。战争把零散的边境摩擦变为对盟邦体系的争夺，罗马在战后以条约与驻军巩固地位，逐步确立对拉丁地区的支配。
statement.en: Conflict broke out between Rome and the cities of the Latin League over the inheritance of Alba Longa.

title.en: Lydian king Alyattes mints the world's first metal coins

summary.en: Around 640 BCE, Alyattes, king of Lydia in Asia Minor, ordered the minting of the world's first coins made of electrum (a gold-silver alloy). These elliptical coins, stamped with a lion's head, weighed about 4.7 grams each. The invention of coinage greatly facilitated commerce, and Lydia's capital Sardis became a commercial center of the ancient world. His son Croesus later min

statement.zh: 公元前640年左右，小亚细亚的吕底亚王国国王阿律阿铁斯（Alyattes）下令铸造了世界上第一批金银混合的琥珀金货币。这些椭圆形钱币表面有狮子头的印记，统一重量约4.7克。货币的发明极大促进了商业交换，吕底亚首都萨迪斯成为古代世界的商业中心。其子克洛伊索斯后来铸造了标准的纯金和纯银硬币。

title.en: Ashurbanipal conquers Elam, captures Susa, and carries off Elamite statues

summary.en: In 639 BCE, Ashurbanipal launched a final, devastating campaign against rebellious Elam. The Assyrian army penetrated deep into Elam, again captured Susa, and plundered the statues of the Elamite goddess Nanaya and others. Ashurbanipal's palace reliefs at Nineveh detailed this campaign. It was Assyria's last major victory; thereafter the empire quickly declined.

title.en: Battle of Hongshui between Song and Chu: Duke Xiang of Song, refusing to attack before the enemy is fully arrayed, suffers a crushing defeat and later dies of his wounds

summary.en: In 638 BCE, Duke Xiang of Song led his army to confront the Chu army at the Hong River (present-day Zhecheng, Henan). The Song army arrived first and formed ranks on the north bank. statement.zh: 公元前638年，宋襄公率宋军在泓水（今河南柘城）与楚军交战。宋军先到北岸列好阵势，楚军正在渡河。大司马公孙固建议趁半渡攻击，宋襄公以君子不困人于厄为由拒绝。楚军全部渡河后正在列阵，公孙固再次请求攻击，宋襄公仍以君子不鼓不成列拒绝。待楚军列阵完毕，宋襄公才下令进攻，宋军大败，襄公腿部中箭。次年因箭伤去世。
statement.en:
In 638 BCE, Duke Xiang of Song led his army to confront the Chu army at the Hong River (present-day Zhecheng, Henan). The Song army arrived first and formed ranks on the north bank. The Chu army was crossing the river. The commander, Gongsun Gu, suggested attacking while they were half across, but Duke Xiang refused, citing the principle that a gentleman does not take advantage of the distressed. After the Chu army had fully crossed and was still forming ranks, Gongsun Gu again pleaded to attack, but Duke Xiang again refused. Only when the Chu army had fully formed did Duke Xiang order the attack. The Song army was routed, and the Duke was hit in the leg by an arrow. He died the following year from his wounds.

For Asia in 638 BCE, “Battle of Hongshui between Song and Chu: Duke Xiang of Song, refusing to attack before the enemy is fully arrayed, suffers a crushing defeat and later dies of his wounds” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Jin prince Chong'er returns to Jin with the support of Duke Mu of Qin and ascends the throne as Duke Wen of Jin

summary.en: In 636 BCE, Prince Chong'er of Jin, after nineteen years of exile, returned to Jin under military escort from Duke Mu of Qin. Duke Mu sent troops to cross the Yellow River and escorted Chong'er to Quwo (present-day Wenxi, Shanxi), where he became Duke Wen of Jin. Chong'er was then 62 years old. After ascending, he employed worthy ministers such as Zhao Cui, Hu Yan, and Xian Zhe

statement.zh: 公元前636年，流亡在外十九年的晋国公子重耳在秦穆公的军事护送下回到晋国。秦穆公派兵送重耳渡过黄河，在曲沃（今山西闻喜）即位为晋文公。重耳时年已62岁。晋文公即位后任用赵衰、狐偃、先轸等贤臣整顿内政、发展军事，晋国迅速崛起为中原强国。四年后（前632年）晋文公在城濮之战大败楚军。
statement.en:
In 636 BCE, Prince Chong'er of Jin, after nineteen years of exile, returned to Jin under military escort from Duke Mu of Qin. Duke Mu sent troops to cross the Yellow River and escorted Chong'er to Quwo (present-day Wenxi, Shanxi), where he became Duke Wen of Jin. Chong'er was then 62 years old. After ascending, he employed worthy ministers such as Zhao Cui, Hu Yan, and Xian Zhen to reorganize internal affairs and develop the military. Jin quickly rose as a major power in the Central Plains. Four years later (632 BCE), Duke Wen defeated Chu at the Battle of Chengpu.

zh: 公元前636年，流亡在外十九年的晋国公子重耳在秦穆公的军事护送下回到晋国。秦穆公派兵送重耳渡过黄河，在曲沃（今山西闻喜）即位为晋文公。重耳时年已62岁。晋文公即位后任用赵衰、狐偃、先轸等贤臣整顿内政、发展军事，晋国迅速崛起为中原强国。四年后（前632年）晋文公在城濮之战大败楚军。
公元前636年，流亡在外十九年的晋国公子重耳在秦穆公的军事护送下回到晋国。
en: In 636 BCE, Prince Chong'er of Jin, after nineteen years of exile, returned to Jin under military escort from Duke Mu of Qin. Duke Mu sent troops to cross the Yellow River and escorted Chong'er to Quwo (present-day Wenxi, Shanxi), where he became Duke Wen of Jin. Chong'er was then 62 years old. After ascending, he employed worthy ministers such as Zhao Cui, Hu Yan, and Xian Zhen to reorganize internal affairs and develop the military. Jin quickly rose as a major power in the Central Plains. Four years later (632 BCE), Duke Wen defeated Chu at the Battle of Chengpu.

title.en: Duke Wen of Jin puts down Prince Dai's rebellion and restores King Xiang of Zhou

summary.en: Prince Dai, allied with the Di, attacked the royal city. King Xiang of Zhou fled to Zheng. Duke Wen of Jin led an army to the king's aid, killed Prince Dai, and escorted King Xiang back to Luoyi. The king granted Yangfan, Wen, Yuan, and other lands to Jin.

statement.zh: 公元前634年，楚成王联合陈、蔡、郑、许等国围攻宋国都城。宋成公向刚刚即位的晋文公求救。晋文公想起当年流亡楚国时曾得到楚王厚待，但又不能坐视宋国被灭。他采纳先轸的建议攻打楚国的盟友曹国和卫国以解宋围，从而引发了晋楚争霸的城濮之战。
statement.en:
In 634 BCE, King Cheng of Chu, allied with Chen, Cai, Zheng, and Xu, besieged Song's capital. Duke Cheng of Song appealed for help to Duke Wen of Jin, who had just ascended. Duke Wen recalled that when he had been exiled in Chu, the Chu king treated him generously. Nevertheless, he could not allow Song to be destroyed. Following Xian Zhen's advice, he attacked Chu's allies Cao and Wei to relieve Song, leading to the Battle of Chengpu that decided the Jin-Chu struggle.

statement.zh: 晋、宋、齐、秦联军与楚、陈、蔡联军战于城濮。晋军退90里避楚锋芒，然后两翼合围，大破楚军。子玉自杀。晋文公献楚俘于周，周王命晋为侯伯，诸侯盟于践土。
statement.en:
The allied armies of Jin, Song, Qi, and Qin fought the combined forces of Chu, Chen, and Cai at Chengpu. The Jin army retreated 90 li to avoid the Chu army's initial momentum, then attacked from both flanks, encircling and defeating them. Ziyu committed suicide. Duke Wen of Jin presented Chu prisoners to the Zhou king, who appointed Jin as the overlord. The feudal lords met at Jiantu.

For Asia in 632 BCE, “Battle of Chengpu: Duke Wen of Jin retreats 90 li (three 'she'), then crushes the Chu army; the Treaty of Jiantu establishes Jin's hegemony” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Greek colonists found Cyrene

summary.en: Around 631 BC, after years of drought and failed harvests, the island of Thera (modern Santorini) sent out colonists on the advice of the Delphic oracle. Led by Battus I they crossed to the Libyan coast and founded Cyrene. The soil was rich and the rainfall generous, and the city grew wealthy, above all on silphium, a prized medicinal herb whose image appeared on its coins. Cyr

title.en: Assyrian king Ashurbanipal dies; the Assyrian Empire rapidly declines

summary.en: Around 631 BCE, Ashurbanipal, the last great king of Assyria, died. He had built a vast empire stretching from Egypt to Iran and founded the famous library at Nineveh. After his death the empire declined rapidly amid internal division, frontier revolts and a combined Median-Babylonian counterattack. Nineveh fell twenty years later, in 612 BCE.

title.en: Birth of the Greek Poet Sappho (circa)

summary.en: The most famous Greek lyric poetess, Sappho, was born on the island of Lesbos; the traditional reliable date is around 630–570 BCE. Her poetry, known for its delicate love imagery and elegant language, greatly influenced later Western poetry.

title.en: Battle of Xiao between Qin and Jin: Jin forces annihilate the Qin army, thwarting Qin's eastward advance

summary.en: Duke Mu of Qin ignored Jian Shu's advice and sent three generals to attack Zheng. On the way, they were discovered by the Zheng merchant Xian Gao, who feigned a welcome. Qin then turned its attention to expanding westward against the Rong.

Qin then turned its attention to expanding westward against the Rong.

title.en: Duke Mu of Qin conquers twelve Rong states in the west, becoming hegemon of the west; the Zhou king sends him a golden drum

summary.en: In 623 BCE, Duke Mu of Qin, following the advice of You Yu, launched a major campaign against the Western Rong. statement.zh: 公元前623年，秦穆公采纳由余的计策，大举征伐西戎。秦军先后攻灭绵诸、翟、豲等十二个戎人国家，辟地1000里，成为西戎地区的霸主。周襄王派召公过送来金鼓表示祝贺，正式承认秦穆公在西戎的霸主地位。秦国的领土和实力因此大增，为日后统一全国奠定了基础。
statement.en:
In 623 BCE, Duke Mu of Qin, following the advice of You Yu, launched a major campaign against the Western Rong. The Qin army conquered twelve Rong states, including Mianzhu, Di, and Huan, expanding territory by a thousand li, and became the hegemon of the western regions. King Xiang of Zhou sent the official Zhao Guo with a golden drum to congratulate him, formally recognizing Duke Mu's hegemony in the west. This greatly increased Qin's territory and power, laying the foundation for its eventual unification of China.

sources.excerpt: Thales of Miletus (born c. 624–620 bce—died c. 548–545 bce) was a philosopher renowned as one of the legendary Seven Wise Men, or Sophoi, of antiquity. title.en: Duke Mu of Qin dies with 177 human sacrifices, including three worthy ministers of the Zi-che family

summary.en: In 621 BCE, Duke Mu of Qin, one of the Five Hegemons, died. He had reigned for 39 years, expanding west and making Qin the hegemon of the west. At his death, following the backward Qin custom of human sacrifice, 177 people were buried with him, including three worthy ministers – Zi-che Yansi, Zi-che Zhongxing, and Zi-che Zhenhu (the 'Three Good Men'). The people of Qin mourned

statement.zh: 公元前621年，春秋五霸之一的秦穆公去世。秦穆公在位39年，向西扩张使秦国成为西方霸主。他去世时按照秦国的落后制度实行人殉，殉葬177人，其中包括三位贤臣——子车奄息、子车仲行、子车针虎（"三良"）。秦国人为之悲恸，《诗经·秦风·黄鸟》即哀悼此事。人殉制度使秦国在人才竞争中处于劣势。
statement.en:
In 621 BCE, Duke Mu of Qin, one of the Five Hegemons, died. He had reigned for 39 years, expanding west and making Qin the hegemon of the west. At his death, following the backward Qin custom of human sacrifice, 177 people were buried with him, including three worthy ministers – Zi-che Yansi, Zi-che Zhongxing, and Zi-che Zhenhu (the 'Three Good Men'). The people of Qin mourned deeply, and the poem 'Yellow Bird' in the Book of Songs mourns this event. The practice of human sacrifice put Qin at a disadvantage in the competition for talent.

For Asia in 621 BCE, “Duke Mu of Qin dies with 177 human sacrifices, including three worthy ministers of the Zi-che family” is a traceable node of Society change whose significance is best read through later events.

zh: 公元前621年，春秋五霸之一的秦穆公去世。秦穆公在位39年，向西扩张使秦国成为西方霸主。他去世时按照秦国的落后制度实行人殉，殉葬177人，其中包括三位贤臣——子车奄息、子车仲行、子车针虎（"三良"）。秦国人为之悲恸，《诗经·秦风·黄鸟》即哀悼此事。人殉制度使秦国在人才竞争中处于劣势。
公元前621年，春秋五霸之一的秦穆公去世。
en: In 621 BCE, Duke Mu of Qin, one of the Five Hegemons, died. He had reigned for 39 years, expanding west and making Qin the hegemon of the west. At his death, following the backward Qin custom of human sacrifice, 177 people were buried with him, including three worthy ministers – Zi-che Yansi, Zi-che Zhongxing, and Zi-che Zhenhu (the 'Three Good Men'). The people of Qin mourned deeply, and the poem 'Yellow Bird' in the Book of Songs mourns this event. The practice of human sacrifice put Qin at a disadvantage in the competition for talent.
In 621 BCE, Duke Mu of Qin, one of the Five Hegemons, died.

title.en: Zhao Dun of Jin takes power, marking the rise of the Zhao clan

summary.en: Duke Xiang of Jin died. Zhao Dun wanted to install Prince Yong but was opposed by Jia Ji. Eventually, the young Yigao was installed as Duke Ling of Jin, with Zhao Dun controlling military and political affairs, beginning the era of ministerial dominance in Jin.

statement.zh:

statement.zh: 公元前619年，周襄王姬郑去世。襄王在位32年，期间齐桓公、晋文公先后称霸，周王室权威进一步衰落。其子姬壬臣继位，是为周顷王。周顷王在位时王室财政极为困难，甚至无力为襄王举办像样的葬礼，不得不向鲁国乞求财政援助。
statement.en:
In 619 BCE, King Xiang of Zhou, Ji Zheng, died. He had reigned for 32 years, during which Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin successively became hegemons, and the Zhou royal authority further declined. His son Ji Renchen succeeded him as King Qing of Zhou. When King Qing came to power, the royal finances were so straitened that he could not afford a proper funeral for King Xiang and had to beg for financial aid from Lu.

For Asia in 619 BCE, “King Xiang of Zhou dies; his son King Qing of Zhou, Ji Renchen, ascends” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

He had reigned for 32 years, during which Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin successively became hegemons, and the Zhou royal authority further declined. His son Ji Renchen succeeded him as King Qing of Zhou. When King Qing came to power, the royal finances were so straitened that he could not afford a proper funeral for King Xiang and had to beg for financial aid from Lu.

title.en: Etruscan Lucumo seizes power in Rome and becomes king, taking the name Tarquinius Priscus

summary.en: The Etruscans, using their wealth and military power, took control of Rome, establishing the Tarquin dynasty. Rome entered a period of Etruscan rule, with major construction projects such as the Cloaca Maxima (Great Sewer).

statement.zh:
伊特鲁里亚人凭借财富和武力控制罗马，建立塔奎尼乌斯王朝，罗马进入伊特鲁里亚统治时期，建筑下水道等大型工程。王朝以工程与仪式塑造城市，排水、广场与神庙建设改变罗马面貌；王权与贵族的关系趋于紧张。外来王朝的统治为共和奠定城市基础。

把「伊特鲁里亚人卢库摩篡位成为罗马国王，改名塔奎尼乌斯·普里斯库斯」放回公元前616年的罗马王国，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: King Zhuang of Chu ascends the throne; after three years of silence, he startles all

statement.zh: 公元前613年，楚穆王去世，其子熊旅继位，是为楚庄王。庄王即位后最初三年沉湎酒色、不理朝政，楚国群臣忧心忡忡。大夫申无畏以"有鸟在阜，三年不蜚不鸣"的寓言进谏。庄王回答说"三年不蜚，蜚将冲天；三年不鸣，鸣将惊人"。从此庄王励精图治，整顿内政、北伐中原，最终问鼎中原成为春秋五霸之一。
statement.en:
In 613 BCE, King Mu of Chu died, and his son Xiong Lü succeeded him as King Zhuang of Chu. For the first three years, King Zhuang was mired in wine and pleasure, neglecting government. The ministers of Chu were worried. The minister Shen Wuwu used the allegory of a bird that does not fly or sing for three years and asked what kind of bird it was. King Zhuang replied, 'For three years it does not fly; when it flies, it will soar to the sky. For three years it does not sing; when it sings, it will startle all.' He then energetically pursued reforms, marched north, and eventually 'inquired about the weight of the Nine Tripods,' becoming one of the Five Hegemons.

For Asia in 613 BCE, “King Zhuang of Chu ascends the throne; after three years of silence, he startles all” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

en: In 613 BCE, King Mu of Chu died, and his son Xiong Lü succeeded him as King Zhuang of Chu. For the first three years, King Zhuang was mired in wine and pleasure, neglecting government. The ministers of Chu were worried. The minister Shen Wuwu used the allegory of a bird that does not fly or sing for three years and asked what kind of bird it was. King Zhuang replied, 'For three years it does not fly; when it flies, it will soar to the sky. For three years it does not sing; when it sings, it will startle all.' He then energetically pursued reforms, marched north, and eventually 'inquired about the weight of the Nine Tripods,' becoming one of the Five Hegemons.

statement.zh: 公元前608年，齐顷公在即位初期为了重振齐桓公时期的霸业，发兵攻打东方的邻国莒国（今山东莒县）。齐军攻占了莒国数个边境城邑。莒国在齐国强大的军事压力下被迫求和称臣，割让部分领土。齐国通过此战扩大了自己在山东半岛东部的势力范围。
statement.en:
In 608 BCE, Duke Qing of Qi, early in his reign, sought to revive the hegemony of Duke Huan of Qi. He attacked the eastern neighbor Ju (present-day Ju County, Shandong). The Qi army captured several border towns of Ju. Under strong military pressure, Ju was forced to sue for peace and become a vassal, ceding some territory. Through this campaign, Qi expanded its sphere of influence in the eastern part of the Shandong Peninsula.

title.en: Zhao Chuan, cousin of Zhao Dun of Jin, assassinates Duke Ling of Jin; Zhao Dun returns and establishes Duke Cheng; the historian records 'Zhao Dun assassinated his ruler'

summary.en: Duke Ling of Jin was cruel and tyrannical. Zhao Dun left the capital to avoid trouble. Before he had crossed the border, Duke Ling was killed. The grand historian Dong Hu wrote in the record: 'Zhao Dun assassinated his ruler.' Zhao Dun had no choice but to establish Prince Heitun as Duke Cheng of Jin.

statement.zh:
晋灵公残虐，赵盾避位出奔，未出境而灵公被杀。太史董狐直书“赵盾弑其君”，赵盾无奈，立公子黑臀为晋成公。灵公因暴虐失众，赵穿起而弑君；董狐以赵盾身为正卿、出奔未越境而返，仍负其责。书法之争成为后世史家讨论直笔的典故。

把「晋赵盾族弟赵穿弑晋灵公，赵盾返晋立成公，史书书“赵盾弑其君”」放回公元前607年的晋，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en:
Duke Ling of Jin was cruel and tyrannical. Zhao Dun left the capital to avoid trouble. Before he had crossed the border, Duke Ling was killed. The grand historian Dong Hu wrote in the record: 'Zhao Dun assassinated his ruler.' Zhao Dun had no choice but to establish Prince Heitun as Duke Cheng of Jin. The duke's cruelty lost him his following and Zhao Chuan killed him; Dong Hu held Zhao Dun responsible as chief minister who fled but did not leave. The case became a byword among later historians for upright record.

Placing “Zhao Chuan, cousin of Zhao Dun of Jin, assassinates Duke Ling of Jin; Zhao Dun returns and establishes Duke Cheng; the historian records 'Zhao Dun assassinated his ruler'” in 607 BCE Asia shows one concrete slice of Politics change.

title.en: Nebuchadnezzar II formally becomes king of Babylon; begins massive building projects

summary.en: In 604 BCE, Nabopolassar, founder of the Neo-Babylonian Empire, died and was succeeded by his son Nebuchadnezzar II. Immediately after ascending, he launched one of the most ambitious building programs in ancient history: construction of the Ishtar Gate, Processional Way, the Hanging Gardens (one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World), Babylon's walls, and huge palace compl

statement.zh: 公元前604年，新巴比伦帝国的缔造者那波帕拉萨尔去世，其子尼布甲尼撒二世继承王位。
statement.en: In 604 BCE, Nabopolassar, founder of the Neo-Babylonian Empire, died and was succeeded by his son Nebuchadnezzar II.

sources.locator: Section on accession and building activity
sources.excerpt: After his father’s death on August 16, 605, Nebuchadnezzar returned to Babylon and ascended the throne within three weeks. ... Nebuchadnezzar’s main activity, other than as military commander, was the rebuilding of Babylon. He completed and extended fortifications begun by his father, built a great moat and a new outer defense wall, paved the ceremonial Processional Way with limestone, rebuilt and embellished the principal temples, and cut canals.

title.en: King Zhuang of Chu attacks Chen, executes Xia Zhengshu, initially intends to annex Chen but later restores it, winning praise from the feudal lords

summary.en: Xia Zhengshu, a minister of Chen, assassinated Duke Ling of Chen. King Zhuang of Chu led an army to punish him, executing Xia Zhengshu by dismemberment. He initially wanted to annex Chen, but following the advice of Shen Shushi, he restored Chen. The feudal lords were impressed and submitted to Chu.

title.en: The Yellow River changes course at Qi County, causing major flooding; vassal states jointly build dikes

summary.en: In 602 BCE, the Yellow River changed its course near Qi County (present-day Qi County, Henan), the first clearly documented course change in history. statement.zh: 公元前602年，黄河在杞县（今河南杞县）附近发生历史上第一次有明确文字记载的改道。原河道在东流至浚县后折向北入渤海，改道后主流东流至滑县后折向东北。改道造成大面积水患，淹没农田和村庄无数。齐、鲁、宋、卫等国被迫联合组织民夫修筑新堤防，这是中国古代各诸侯国首次联合治理黄河。
statement.en:
In 602 BCE, the Yellow River changed its course near Qi County (present-day Qi County, Henan), the first clearly documented course change in history. The original course flowed east to Xun County then north into the Bohai Sea. After the change, the main stream flowed east to Hua County then turned northeast. The change caused widespread flooding, submerging farmland and villages. The states of Qi, Lu, Song, and Wei were forced to organize laborers to build new dikes, the first joint effort by Chinese states to control the Yellow River.

In 602 BCE, “The Yellow River changes course at Qi County, causing major flooding; vassal states jointly build dikes” belongs to the field of Disaster in Asia.

title.en: Greek lyric poet Sappho flourishes on Lesbos, composing love poetry

summary.en: Around 600 BCE, the most famous female poet of ancient Greece, Sappho, composed lyric poetry in Mytilene on the island of Lesbos. Sappho ran a school for aristocratic girls teaching poetry and music. Her poetry, especially love poetry, was emotional and refined, leading Plato to call her the 'Tenth Muse'. Sappho was highly esteemed in ancient Greece, creating the Sapphic stanza

title.en: King Zhuang of Chu defeats Jin at the Battle of Bi, establishing Chu's hegemony

summary.en: King Zhuang of Chu led an army to attack Zheng; Duke Jing of Jin sent Xun Linfu to rescue Zheng. The Jin army was divided internally. The Chu army launched a surprise attack while the Jin army was crossing the river, routing them. After the Battle of Bi, King Zhuang of Chu became hegemon.

title.en: Sushruta compiles the Sushruta Samhita

summary.en: The ancient Indian surgeon Sushruta compiles the Sushruta Samhita, recording plastic surgery, cataract and suturing techniques, regarded as a founder of surgery.

statement.zh:
古印度外科医家苏斯鲁塔编成《妙闻集》，记载整形、白内障等外科手术与缝合技术，被视为外科鼻祖。把这些手术类别放在同一部医书中，说明当时的外科知识已被系统整理，而不只是零散经验；整形与白内障手术尤其要求对组织层次和器械操作有稳定认识。

把「苏斯鲁塔撰成《妙闻集》」放回公元前600年的印度，可以看到医学变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en: Susruta, an ancient Indian surgeon, compiled the "Collection of Wonderful Information", recording surgical operations and suturing techniques such as plastic surgery and cataract, and is regarded as the originator of surgery.

statement.en:
Egyptian Pharaoh Necho II (r. 610–595 BCE) sponsored a fleet of Phoenician sailors who set out from the Red Sea and sailed south along Africa's east coast. Each autumn they went ashore to sow and harvest grain before continuing. After about three years, they returned to Egypt via the Strait of Gibraltar, completing the first recorded circumnavigation of Africa and proving that the continent is surrounded by sea.

For Africa in 600 BCE, “Phoenician fleet completes circumnavigation of Africa” is a traceable node of Exploration change whose significance is best read through later events.
